n is a sum of two squares iff every prime p ≡ 3 (mod 4) divides n to an even power. Write n = j²·u uniquely, where j is composed only of primes ≡ 3 (mod 4) and u has no prime factor ≡ 3 (mod 4). Then count = Σ_j A(⌊2026/j²⌋), where A(x) = #{u ≤ x : u has no prime factor ≡ 3 mod 4}.

Admissible j ≤ 45: 1, 3, 7, 9, 11, 19, 21, 23, 27, 31, 33, 43. Bounds: 2026, 225, 41, 25, 16, 5, 4, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1.

To get A(x), let C(y) = # odd v ≤ y all of whose prime factors are ≡ 1 (mod 4) (v = 1 included); then A(x) = Σ_{k≥0} C(x/2^k).
Computed (primes ≡ 1 mod 4 counted by listing primes and reducing mod 4, composites enumerated as 5·v, 13·v, 17·v, 29·v, 37·v, 41·v with v in the appropriate range):
C(1)=1, C(3)=1, C(7)=2, C(15)=3, C(31)=6, C(63)=10, C(126)=19 (6 primes + 65,85,125), C(253)=34 (+10 primes, +145,169,185,205,221), C(506)=66 (+20 primes, +12 composites: 265,289,305,325,365,377,425,445,481,485,493,505), C(1013)=125 (+38 primes, +21 composites: 13 multiples of 5, 533,689,793,949, 629,697,901, 841), C(2026)=238 (+66 primes ≡1 mod 4 in (1013,2026], +47 composites: 25 multiples of 5 [5·v, v∈(202,405]], 7 of form 13·v, 7 of form 17·v, 4 of form 29·v, 3 of form 37·v, 1681).
A(2026) = 238+125+66+34+19+10+6+3+2+1+1 = 505.
A(225) = 69 (verified two ways: direct listing, and C(225)+C(112)+C(56)+C(28)+C(14)+C(7)+C(3)+C(1) = 31+17+9+5+3+2+1+1).
A(41)=18, A(25)=11, A(16)=8, A(5)=4, A(4)=3, A(3)=2, A(2)=2, A(1)=1.

Check: the same method for N=1000 gives A(1000)=264, A(111)=38, A(20)=10, A(12)=6, A(8)=5, 2+2+1+1+1 → 330, matching the known count of sums of two squares ≤ 1000. Also prime counts check: 82 primes ≡1 (mod 4) up to 1013 (80 up to 1000, known Chebyshev-bias data) and 148 up to 2026 vs π(2026)=306.

Total = 505 + 69 + 18 + 11 + 8 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 626.
